title: NaN compares greater than every other float
description: DuckDB departs from IEEE 754 in one point: NaN compares equal to NaN and greater than any other floating-point number, `+inf` included (`'nan' > sqrt(2)` is true). So `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE` have a total order, and `greatest` and `least` treat NaN as the largest value.
The docs state this for both floating-point types. They say nothing about the sign of a NaN in comparisons (duckdb-nan-equality: `nan = -nan` is true).
`min`, `max` and `quantile_cont` take the values in this order ("in the specified order"); the docs do not restate NaN's place for each aggregate. duckdb-quantile-disc probes `agg.order` for `fp64`.

Round 4 (probes): `median` and `quantile_cont` sort NaN above every number: of 1, 2, NaN, 3 the median is 2.5, `quantile_cont(x, 0.75)` and `quantile_cont(x, 1.0)` are NaN and `quantile_disc(x, 0.75)` is 3.0; of 1, NaN the median is NaN.
reference: `nan_order: GREATEST`, NaN above `+inf`, for sorting, `MIN`, `MAX`, `<`, `greatest` and `least` (docs/core-semantics.md). Substrait's comparisons are IEEE (`NaN < x` false); ST-4 records the gap.

evidence.note: Floating-Point Types: DuckDB follows IEEE 754 for Infinity, -Infinity and NaN with one exception, NaN compares equal to NaN and greater than any other floating point number; example `'nan' > sqrt(2)` is true
NaN Values: 'NaN'::FLOAT = 'NaN'::FLOAT and 'NaN'::FLOAT > 3 give floating point types a total order (beware the consequences for greatest / least)
quantile_cont: the value at a position in the specified order; min and max

provenance.notes: The same sentence of the numeric types page, read for MIN, MAX and quantiles.

evidence.note: EqualsFloat, GreaterThanFloat, GreaterThanEqualsFloat, ComparatorFloat: NaN equals NaN and is greater than every other value, for float and double
sort keys: every NaN encodes to the top key, above +inf

provenance.notes: Confirms `cmp` for fp32 and fp64; the aggregate rows stay at docs.

evidence.note: for FLOAT and DOUBLE: `nan = nan` true; `f > 0` returns 1 and nan; `f > 'nan'` nothing; `f >= 'nan'` nan; `f < 'nan'` 1
ORDER BY puts nan after inf ascending and first descending, also in top-n; `f > 0` counts the NaNs
`(-x) > 0` and `>= 0` true, `< 0` false for NaN and -NaN (VARCHAR results); `(-f) >= 0` over x::FLOAT counts both NaNs
MIN and MAX of FLOAT and DOUBLE: MAX is nan and MIN skips it, in any arrival order and grouped (agg.order, fp32)

provenance.notes: The comparisons and the sort put NaN above +inf at both widths. `quantile_cont` has no NaN test, so the `agg.quant` row stays at the docs.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 4 (probes; duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64)
provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations --write` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows or the error as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 5 (sverify_dev.duckdb_fuzz on homelab, Linux x86_64, budget 900 s per target)
provenance.notes: float_special: 16810 random DuckDB queries over DOUBLE columns and literals holding ±0, NaN, ±inf, 1.7e308, 0.1 and a subnormal, with + - * / %, negation, abs, CASE, COALESCE and comparisons; Rel.eval under DuckDB's semantics agreed with DuckDB on every one (doubles compared to six decimals, so zero and NaN signs are not seen). The one disagreement is integer `i // i` at 0 (DuckDB raises).
